text: UKG, formerly Ultimate Software, lays off 950 employees, many from South Florida offices Cindy Krischer Goodman, South Florida Sun-Sentinel April 16, 2026 3 min read As many as 950 employees of Ultimate Kronos Group (UKG), many of them from offices in Sunrise and Weston, were notified on Wednesday that their jobs would be eliminated in an apparent global restructuring. Layoff notifications were emailed on April 15 by the human resources and workforce management giant that was known as Ultimate Software until it merged with Kronos in 2020. One affected employee posted the layoff notification on the social media platform Reddit . It reads: "950 employees will be exiting the company, with close to 600 employees leaving immediately, while roughly 350 will be asked to remain with UKG for a defined transition period to ensure continuity for our customers and partners as we evolve our operations and service model." UKG brought in a new chief executive officer in 2024, Jennifer Morgan, who has been transforming the company and restructuring operations to create what they're calling an "AI-first company." That transformation has included layoffs and the relocation of some jobs overseas, likely to India, where it already has a presence. "As part of UKG's ongoing transformation, we are restructuring parts of our workforce, impacting approximately 950 employees worldwide, or 6% of our workforce," UKG said in a statement sent to the South Florida Sun Sentinel. "These actions span multiple functions and regions and reflect rapidly evolving market shifts — including changes in technology driven by AI, customer expectations, and how software companies compete — and will better align our structure, skills, and investments for the future. We continually balance competing investments to enhance our market position and evaluate how we operate and align our teams to support customers." The statement added: "We are committed to providing impacted employees with care, dignity, and comprehensive transition resources, while continuing to serve our customers with the mission‑critical solutions they rely on." UKG did not respond to inquiries about the exact number of employees affected in South Florida. Ultimate Software has deep roots in Broward County. It was founded in 1990 by Scott Scherr, who emphasized culture and gave employees stock when they joined. In 2019, Hellman & Friedman, a large San Francisco-based private equity firm, acquired Ultimate Software for $11 billion . The firm merged Ultimate with Kronos a year later, combining two major players in the HR and workforce technology space: Kronos, known for time clocks and scheduling systems, and Ultimate Software, a global provider of HR and payroll solutions. Story Continues UKG laid off 14% of its workforce in late 2024, or about 2,200 of its 15,000 global employees. A South Florida employee told the Sun Sentinel that some longtime staff walked out of the building with their boxed belongings, rattling those who still had jobs. On Wednesday, staff were told not to come to the office as layoff notices arrived by email. According to the memo posted on Reddit, the company wrote: "As we prepare to support each other with care, empathy, and respect, please plan to work from home tomorrow." Dozens of UKG staff members posted on LinkedIn on Thursday that they are open to new employment. Some said they are taking a pause. "I was impacted today by the structural layoffs at UKG," Juan D., a Fort Lauderdale data transfer consultant, said on LinkedIn. "I am going to take some time to reset and figure out next steps." While UKG remains a private company, analysts believe the moves made by the new CEO suggest that the company is preparing for a public offering in the near future. "UKG has now shed about one third of their team since PE took them over, and now they are looking more profitable, and I would bet gearing up for an IPO later this year or next," Anthony Presley, an expert in leadership in the technology sector, said in a LinkedIn post . However, the company disputed that characterization. "UKG actually has more employees today than it did at the time of the Ultimate/Kronos merger," said Domenic Locapo, senior director of public relations for UKG.
